World.title: UK Travel Advisory: Nasarawa Government welcomes exclusion
World.content:
By Edwin Phillip, Lafia

LAFIA: The Nasarawa State Government has welcomed its exclusion from the latest United Kingdom travel advisory, describing the development as a reflection of the state’s efforts to maintain peace and security.

Nasarawa is reportedly the only state in the North-Central region not included in the advisory restricting travel to the region.

The state government said the development demonstrated that its sustained efforts to prevent insecurity and maintain peace were yielding positive results, adding that it would intensify measures to sustain and improve the prevailing security situation.

This was contained in a statement issued on Friday by the Chief Press Secretary to Governor Abdullahi Sule, Mr Ibrahim Addra.

According to the statement, the advisory, which was “still current as at 21st August 2026” on the UK Government website, was issued through the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO).

It said the advisory advised against all but essential travel to states in the North-Central region, with Nasarawa excluded.

The government said it received the development with humility and gratitude to God, adding that it was encouraged by the collective efforts of stakeholders to promote peace and security in the state.

While commending President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, other governors and security agencies for their efforts in tackling security challenges across the country, the government acknowledged that more needed to be done.

It said it would continue to work to sustain and improve the prevailing peace and security in Nasarawa State.

“In Nasarawa, this positive outcome is also a reflection of the deliberate measures taken by the administration of Governor Abdullahi A. Sule to strengthen security, support security agencies and foster closer collaboration with communities and other stakeholders,” the statement said.

Governor Sule appealed to residents to remain vigilant and continue supporting security agencies by providing timely and credible information that could assist in preventing crime and maintaining peace.

World.title: Imo Performs First Robotic-assisted Surgery
World.content:
·Uzodimma: Landmark procedure will make advanced healthcare more accessible, affordable

Imo State has recorded a major breakthrough in healthcare delivery with the successful completion of its first robotic-assisted surgery, making it the first such procedure to be performed in the region east of the Niger.

The landmark operation was carried out yesterday at the Imo Robotics and Oncology Centre (IROC), located within the Imo Specialist Hospital Complex, Umuguma, Owerri, according to a statement by the Chief Press Secretary/Special Adviser Media to the Governor, Oguwike Nwachuku.

The procedure was performed by a team of Nigerian and international medical specialists led by Professor Kingsley Ekwueme, a UK-based consultant robotic and laparoscopic surgeon and an indigene of Imo State.

Addressing journalists after the operation, Ekwueme described the procedure as a complete success, stressing that robotic-assisted surgery offered significant advantages, particularly in the treatment of localised prostate cancer.

According to him, the technology enables surgeons to remove cancerous tissues with greater precision while preserving vital functions, including urinary and erectile control.

“The success rate of robotic surgery for cancer, especially prostate cancer, is phenomenal,” Ekwueme said, adding that patients should not have to endure prolonged incontinence or loss of sexual function following prostate surgery.

Governor Uzodimma, who witnessed the landmark procedure, described it as a major step towards providing residents with quality and affordable specialised healthcare within the state.

He said the facility would serve not only as a treatment centre but also as a platform for early detection and prevention of diseases through routine medical examinations.

“The real measure of success will be in the patients treated, the skills transferred, the specialists developed, the lives improved, and the confidence that our people build in our local healthcare system,” Uzodimma said.

The governor disclosed that the centre operates under a Public-Private Partnership (PPP), with the private sector providing the majority of the funding, a model he said would help guarantee the sustainability and quality management of the facility.

He urged residents to enrol in the Imo State Health Insurance Scheme to make advanced medical treatment more affordable and accessible.

Uzodimma had, ahead of the procedure, described the planned surgery as a major healthcare breakthrough and a product of strategic investments by his administration to transform medical care in the state.

He said the operation was led by Ekwueme alongside an international team of medical specialists from Europe and the United States.

The governor stressed that the establishment of the centre was not solely about acquiring sophisticated equipment, but also about developing the expertise required to operate and sustain the technology locally.

“Our plan has never been to acquire sophisticated medical equipment and leave it idle. Equipment must be matched with competence, and technology must be matched with training,” he said.

Uzodimma explained that robotic-assisted techniques offered greater precision, minimal invasiveness, reduced blood loss and faster recovery for patients.

He added that IROC formed part of a broader upgrade of the Imo Specialist Hospital Complex, which now includes expanded intensive care units, advanced diagnostic facilities, modern surgical theatres, neonatal care and specialised oncology departments.

The governor reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to expanding access to specialised healthcare through the Imo Health Insurance Scheme.

He said the state would continue to invest in healthcare infrastructure and human capital to position Imo as a destination for specialised medical treatment.

“This milestone is merely the beginning of Imo State’s journey toward becoming a premier destination for specialised medical care,” he said.

World.title: Osun Guber: APC Candidate, Oyebamiji Visits Tinubu At State House
World.content:
.Says party reviewing results, to announce next move shortly

.Tasks supporters to remain calm, amid fresh attacks on party members

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

The All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate in the August 15, 2026 governorship poll in Osun State, Asiwaju Bola Oyebamiji, yesterday met with his party’s national leader, President Bola Tinubu at the State House, Abuja.

Speaking with journalists after the closed-door meeting, Oyebamiji popularly known as AMBO, said his party is presently reviewing the outcome of the election and will soon make its next line of action known after completing its assessment.

Oyebamiji, who lost the election to incumbent Governor Ademola Adeleke of Accord Party,

explained that the party had not reached a final decision on the election, urging its members and supporters to remain calm while the review continues.

He said, “For now, the APC is still examining the books, and by the time we spread our sheets, we’ll be able to get back to the public on what our own opinions and what decisions we want to take, but the take home is that they should be calm.”

Though Oyebamiji did not disclose the specific issues being examined by the APC or state whether the party was contemplating a legal challenge to the outcome, he, however, said its position would be communicated to the public after the exercise.

Oyebamiji emphasised that whatever decisions taken from the review, peace must remain paramount, describing government and politics as ultimately being about the welfare of the people.

“The most important thing is to run every election with peaceful mind. It is important for us that we Nigerians have to know that government is about people, and it’s about people, and it’s about people, and because it’s about people, it is important that we need to be peaceful and I want to appeal to our people in Osun that they need to be peaceful,” he said.

The APC candidate also raised concerns over what he called continuing attacks on APC members in Osun following the election.

He appealed directly to Governor Adeleke to call his supporters to order, warning that post-election violence could undermine peace in the state.

“I want to advise the governor that it’s important for him to talk to his people. Violence against our people is not too good, and he needs to talk to them so that each and every one of us can be on the same page.”

On allegations of attacks on APC members which he had raised in his initial reaction to the election results, Oyebamiji claimed that fresh incidents were recorded on Friday morning.

According to him, between four and five people were attacked in his hometown, Ikire, adding that security agencies had been notified.

“Well, yes. Even as at this morning, in my own village, Ikire, some were attacked; about four, five people were attacked. We have informed the security operatives accordingly. That’s what I have to say about that,” Oyebamiji said.

Despite the allegations, the APC candidate repeatedly appealed to his supporters to remain peaceful while awaiting the party’s decision on the election.

Oyebamiji’s meeting with the President came a day after the Osun Governor was received by the President at the State House.

Adeleke had, after Thursday’s closed-door meeting, thanked Tinubu for his commitment to a free and fair electoral process in Osun.

World.title: Alleged Cybercrime: Olukoyede Orders Withdrawal of Charges against Maryam Shehu, Abubakar Abdulhamad
World.content:
Alex Enumah in Abuja

The Executive Chairman of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), Mr. Ola Olukoyede, has ordered the withdrawal of charges preferred against Maryam Isah Shehu and Abubakar Shuraim Abdulhamad.

Both were arraigned on Thursday before Justice Joyce Abdulmalik of a Federal High Court, Abuja, on allegations bordering on cybercrime and peddling malicious information against the commission.

However, barely 21 hours after their arraignment, the anti-graft agency boss ordered the withdrawal of the charges against them on compassionate grounds, a statement from the spokesperson of the commission, Dele Oyewale, disclosed yesterday.

He stated that while the commission considered the arraignment of the two defendants for cyber stalking to be contrary to Section 24(2) (c) of the Cybercrimes (Prohibition, Prevention, Etc) Act, 2015 (As Amended) 2024 and punishable under Section 24 (2) (c) (ii) of the same Act, the Executive Chairman, nonetheless, considered the passionate pleas and apologies of Shehu’s father and appeals of well-meaning Nigerians for leniency.

“To this end, he has directed that charges filed against the two young Nigerians be dropped and warned that the EFCC would no longer tolerate any wilful attack on its image in any form, medium or platform.

“The EFCC’s boss assured Nigerians that the Commission would continue to function in line with its assigned mandate and in the best interests of the nation,” the statement read in part.

World.title: NDIC: Depositors of 46 Revoked MFBs Protected, Payments Ongoing
World.content:
Nume Ekeghe

The Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation (NDIC), Mr. Thompson Oludare, has assured depositors of microfinance banks (MFBs) whose licences were revoked by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) that they remain protected under the country’s deposit insurance framework, as the corporation continues payment of the guaranteed portion of their deposits.

The Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, NDIC, Mr. Thompson Oludare, said the corporation was still paying eligible depositors of the 46 MFBs whose licences were revoked by the CBN on July 1, 2026.

Oludare said the payment process was ongoing and that the corporation could not yet provide a final figure for the number of depositors paid, as new beneficiaries continued to be identified and processed.

Oludare said this yesterday at a three-day workshop for senior management and executive staff of the NDIC, organised in collaboration with the Bureau of Public Procurement (BPP).

He said, “As we speak, we have started paying the depositors. That’s the guaranteed portion of their deposits. It’s an ongoing process, and it is difficult to put numbers because even as I speak with you today, Friday, I’m sure new depositors are being paid,” he said.

He explained that the NDIC was leveraging Bank Verification Numbers (BVNs), in collaboration with the Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System (NIBSS), to identify affected depositors and locate their alternative accounts in other banks for direct payment.

According to him, the approach was designed to make the process seamless and eliminate the need for depositors to appear physically before the corporation for verification.

“All we need to do is to make sure that the accounts that have BVNs, that’s the Bank Verification Number identified, and in collaboration with the NIBSS, Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System, we identify their alternative accounts in other banks and pay them seamlessly without their having to come to us for verification.”

The NDIC chief said the ongoing exercise was part of the corporation’s mandate to protect depositors and sustain confidence in the financial system, noting that financial institution failures, while undesirable, could occur.

He said the objective of the deposit insurance system was to ensure that customers were not left without protection when such failures occurred.

“Our expectation is that you have a country where deposit insurance is pervasive, where people know that their deposits with the banks are guaranteed and safe.

“We do not expect institutions to fail, but then it is a fact of life. Just as people will die, some institutions will fail. But when they do, we want depositors to be sure that they are covered by the NDIC.”

At the workshop, the Director General/Chief Executive Officer of the BPP, Dr. Adebowale A. Adedokun, disclosed that the federal government saved N400 billion in the first six to seven months of 2026 through its price intelligence and benchmarking system.

Adedokun said the mechanism had also generated N1.1 trillion in savings for the government in 2025.

He explained that the BPP benchmarks procurement requests and project costs submitted by government agencies against prevailing market prices before approval, allowing the bureau to identify excessive pricing and reduce procurement costs.

According to him, the savings represent funds that would otherwise have been spent on inflated procurement costs and can now remain available to government agencies for other priorities.

Adedokun said the introduction of price intelligence had also increased awareness among contractors and government agencies, while strengthening technical scrutiny of public procurement.

“The most important thing is the awareness that has been brought into the system, the technical prudency that has been produced is beginning to give governments not only savings and also demanding that contractors do a good job,” he said.

World.title: Wike: Adeleke Now Part of Tinubu’s National Rainbow Coalition
World.content:
.Adeleke won’t join APC, will work with FG, says campaign spokesman

.Osun poll: lawyers give INEC, police seven-day ultimatum to probe alleged inciting statements, killings

Olawale Ajimotokan and Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, said the visit of Osun State Governor Ademola Adeleke to President Bola Tinubu was part of a plan to build a larger Rainbow Coalition in support of the aspiration of the President in the 2027 election.

Wike stated this yesterday in Abuja during an inspection of the IBB International Golf and Country Club that was ongoing renovation.

However, the spokesperson for the Ademola Adeleke Campaign Council, Pelumi Olajengbesi, has dismissed speculation that Governor Adeleke may defect to the All Progressives Congress (APC), saying the governor’s recent meeting with President Bola Tinubu was a courtesy visit and not a prelude to changing political allegiance.

He said although Adeleke was in another political party, Wike dismissed claims by rival factions regarding the newly re-elected governor’s platform strategy, noting that while Adeleke ran on the Accord Party platform due to internal wranglings within the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), he remains deeply rooted in the PDP structure and is now fully committed to supporting Tinubu ahead of 2027.

Wike said, “l don’t know what you call opposition as far as there is no opposition now. Adeleke is only… You remember PDP, you realise that. But because of internal wranglings, and for him to be able to secure a ticket to run for the second term, he had to find a platform, and that platform happened to be Accord Party. But he’s a member of the Peoples Democratic Party.

“And what happened last night (Thursday) is meeting to rebuild a larger Rainbow Coalition. And he is supporting Mr. President. He’s in a different party; I’m supporting Mr. President, and I’m in a different party. So, it’s a larger Rainbow Coalition. I told you that the 2027 election will be the easiest election. All those ADC who are talking about ‘Oh, they helped Adeleke to win,’ they just wanted to go and harvest where they never planted, you know.

“So, Adeleke is fully supporting Mr. President. And so, we had to meet last night and encourage ourselves to continue. And the next few weeks, watch what is going to happen. You will see a larger Rainbow Coalition in this country.”

The also reiterated that his strategy was to keep political rivals like Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi, off-balance, adding that their discomfort over these political realignments gives him no concern.

“I have told you—when you say “leading opposition” that there’s no opposition. What you have are people who are just trying to see whether they can be relevant. Who is the opposition leader now, who? Ordinarily, it should have been PDP, but because of the crisis we’ve had, and so you can’t see a formidable party that you will call the leading opposition party. So, I don’t care. Whatever—whatever they feel is not my business. I don’t want them to feel well. It’s not my wish that they should feel well. My business is to make them not feel well all the time.

“If they are having high blood pressures, yes, that’s my job—to make them have high blood pressure. Your business is to make sure that you beat him thoroughly, so that he will be sick all through. And that’s what we are doing to them. So, how Atiku feels, how Obi feels, ah, it does not give me any headache. In fact, if I know now how they feel, I will add more crises for them. So, that’s my position.”

Wike also reaffirmed that the President has directed that the rehabilitation of IBB International Golf and Country Club be completed and the facility reopened to the public in December.

Meanwhile, Olajengbesi who spoke with journalists in Abuja yesterday, said Adeleke remained committed to the Accord Party but would work with the federal government to advance the interests of Osun State and Nigeria.

His clarification came amid growing speculation over the governor’s political future following his separate visits to Tinubu and the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Wike, in Abuja after his victory in the recent Osun State governorship election.

According to him, Adeleke’s visit to the President was in keeping with the principles of Nigeria’s federal system and was intended to demonstrate respect for the office of the President.

“The visit of Governor Ademola Adeleke to the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria is the proper thing to do. It is the norm; it is the standard.

“We all agree that Nigeria is a federation. We have three tiers of government — the federal government, the state government and, of course, the local government.

“Osun State is a sub-nation now under the Nigerian government, and we don’t intend to take Osun State out of Nigeria. So we understand, and I think the governor deemed it necessary to pay a courtesy call to Mr. President as a sign of respect to the office of the President,” Olajengbesi said.

He added that Adeleke used the meeting to commend Tinubu for allowing democratic institutions to function during the governorship election, which, he said, gave Osun voters the opportunity to freely express their choice.

The campaign spokesman said the governor also urged the President to support measures aimed at strengthening democratic institutions and preventing their manipulation by political actors.

He said the meeting was also an opportunity for the governor to promote reconciliation and healing in the state following a tense election.

“The visit of Mr. Governor to Mr. President is not taking the people of Osun State for granted, but the intention is to amplify the aspiration of the people of Osun State,” he said.

Olajengbesi stressed that Adeleke’s victory was primarily the result of the support of Osun voters, rather than the backing of another political party.

He said the governor’s administration had earned public support through its interventions in infrastructure, welfare and other areas of governance.

“The election is about the people coming out en masse to support a governor who has diligently worked for them.

“If you look at the records of Governor Ademola Adeleke, you look at infrastructural development, you look at his intervention in terms of welfare and the needs of people. We have never had a governor before who has prioritised the welfare of the people, who have been so selfless like Governor Ademola Adeleke,” he said.

He was, however, categorical that the governor had no intention of joining the APC.

“The essence of that visit has nothing to do with Governor Ademola Adeleke joining APC. It’s an impossibility. Governor Ademola Adeleke is not joining APC.

“But I can assure you that Governor Ademola Adeleke will work with the Federal Government to ensure that there’s progress in Nigeria and, of course, in Osun State,” Olajengbesi said.

He also dismissed reports that the African Democratic Congress (ADC) collaborated with Adeleke’s campaign during the election.

According to him, Adeleke’s campaign did not seek the support of any political party and remained focused on its own political structure.

“ADC did not reach out to us. We are not interested in collaborating with any political party,” he said.

Olajengbesi said the ADC’s deployment of prominent politicians to Osun during the election did not determine the outcome, insisting that Adeleke won through the backing of the electorate.

His comments came against the backdrop of fresh concerns over the conduct of the election, particularly allegations of inflammatory statements, voter intimidation and politically motivated violence.

The Coalition of Public Interest Lawyers and Advocates (COPA), in a separate development yesterday, gave the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and the Nigeria Police Force a seven-day ultimatum to investigate alleged inciting statements and killings linked to the Osun governorship election.

The National Coordinator of COPA, Ajibola Bello, told journalists in Abuja that the allegations could not be swept aside simply because the election had been concluded.

He said the coalition had reviewed videos allegedly showing political actors threatening opponents, discouraging citizens from voting and, in one instance, calling for the killing of members of an opposition political party.

Bello said COPA was particularly concerned that violence subsequently occurred in some communities where some of the alleged statements were made or directed, with several persons reportedly killed.

He stressed that the conclusion of an election could not extinguish criminal liability where credible evidence existed of offences committed before or during the poll.

The coalition cited a video allegedly attributed to a leading figure in the APC governorship campaign in which the speaker was said to have warned political opponents in Yoruba against acting contrary to the interests of President Tinubu.

Bello said the statement, which he said was made at the beginning of the campaign, was followed by political violence in Esa-Oke, including the killing of a resident.

He, however, cautioned that COPA was not concluding that the statement alone established criminal responsibility for any subsequent killing.

“That determination belongs to investigators and ultimately the courts,” he said, insisting that the allegation and the violence that followed warranted a thorough and impartial investigation.

The lawyers also raised concerns over another video allegedly showing a serving senator calling on supporters to kill members of the Accord Party.

Bello described the allegation as grave, particularly because the person involved was a serving member of the National Assembly.

He said the alleged statement was followed by serious political violence in Ilesa and surrounding communities, where more than nine people were reportedly killed.

“Where a serving Senator is recorded allegedly telling supporters to kill members of an opposing political party, and people subsequently lose their lives in election-related violence, the institutions established by law cannot simply look away,” Bello said.

He stressed that the coalition was not asking the authorities to pronounce anyone guilty, but to investigate the allegations and prosecute where the evidence met the required legal threshold.

COPA also cited another video allegedly involving Francis Eniade, who was purportedly heard warning non-APC members against coming out to vote and specifically mentioning the Speaker of the Osun State House of Assembly, Adewale Egbedun.

Bello argued that no political actor had the authority to determine who could exercise the constitutional right to vote.

He said threats, intimidation and attempts to prevent citizens from voting because of their political affiliation constituted serious threats to democratic governance and potentially violated provisions of the Electoral Act 2026 and other applicable laws.

Bello specifically challenged INEC to exercise its statutory responsibilities in dealing with electoral offences, citing Section 148(2) of the Electoral Act 2026, which provides for the prosecution of offences under the Act by legal officers of INEC or legal practitioners appointed by the commission.

He urged the electoral body not to leave the matter entirely to the police and other security agencies.

The coalition asked the police and relevant security agencies to authenticate the videos, identify and interview those involved, question witnesses and establish the circumstances surrounding the reported killings and other acts of violence.

It further demanded that investigation files be forwarded for prosecution where sufficient evidence was established.

“There can therefore be no institutional buck-passing,” Bello said.

COPA also expressed concern over allegations that political affiliation could be shielding some suspects from investigation or prosecution.

Bello challenged INEC and the police to disprove such allegations through impartial enforcement of the law.

“The easiest way to disprove an allegation of selective justice is to enforce the law without fear or favour,” he said.

The coalition consequently demanded that INEC exercise its prosecutorial powers under Section 148 of the Electoral Act 2026 and ensure that anyone against whom sufficient evidence of an offence exists is brought before a competent court.

“We are demanding investigation, prosecution where the evidence meets the legal threshold, and determination of guilt or innocence by a court of competent jurisdiction,” Bello said.

The two developments have placed renewed focus on the political aftermath of the Osun election, with Adeleke’s camp seeking to project a posture of cooperation with the federal government while rejecting speculation of an APC defection, even as civil society lawyers demand accountability over alleged electoral violence and inflammatory political statements.

World.title: Abiodun Receives PDP, ADC Defectors into APC, Mobilises Ogun East for 2027
World.content:
Ogun State Governor and leader of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Prince Dapo Abiodun, yesterday formally welcomed hundreds of former members of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) and African Democratic Congress (ADC), including party leaders across the nine local government areas of Ogun East Senatorial District, into the ruling APC.

The defectors were received at an elaborate reception held at the Ojude-Oba carnival ground in Ijebu-Ode, which was filled to capacity with APC members, supporters and the new entrants.

Welcoming the defectors, Governor Abiodun described their decision to join the APC as a demonstration that they had “seen the light”, assuring them of equal treatment and full integration into the party.

“We are happy you have seen the light and you have decided to follow the light. You have become one of us from now on,” he said.

The governor urged the new and existing members to return to their respective wards and mobilise support for the APC ahead of the 2027 general elections, expressing confidence that the party would retain its dominance in the state.

Abiodun said the achievements of his administration since 2019 had distinguished the APC from opposition parties, particularly in the area of infrastructure, noting that more than 100 roads had been constructed across Ogun East, including about 26 roads in Ijebu-Ode alone.

He listed some of the ongoing and completed projects in the senatorial district to include the Gateway International Airport, major road projects, the Olokola Deep Sea Port, the Olokola-Kajola Gas Industrial Free Zone, oil exploration in Ogun Waterside and other economic infrastructure.

The governor also announced that the reconstruction of the Ago-Iwoye–Ibadan Road would be flagged off on Monday alongside the Minister of Works, Senator Dave Umahi.

According to him, the road runs from Ijebu-Ode through Ago-Iwoye to Ibadan and is one of the projects secured through the support of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.

Abiodun further disclosed that his administration had awarded the reconstruction of the Ilishan–Ago-Iwoye–Ijebu-Igbo Road, as well as the Okun-Owa Road, Aiyepe–Odogbolu Road and Ikenne–Aiyepe Road.

“Help me to ask them if they have ever done even a kilometre of road?” the governor challenged, referring to opposition parties.

He said the APC’s record of performance had left the opposition with little to campaign ahead of 2027.

“Anyone just making any baseless noise is just lying to you, because in 2019, they fell, in 2023, they also fell and I am certain that in 2027, they will also fail,” he said.

The governor also expressed optimism that Ogun would soon join the league of oil-producing states, while noting that the development of the Olokola Deep Sea Port and revival of the OKNLG project would further transform Ogun East and strengthen the state’s economy.

Abiodun commended President Tinubu for his support for Ogun State, particularly in the area of infrastructure, saying the President’s administration had demonstrated commitment to the development of the state.

He said he believed that the people of the South-west would support President Tinubu in 2027 based on his achievements in infrastructure and economic development.

“Every son and daughter of the South-west will vote for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in 2027, not because he is a son of the soil, but because of his antecedents in developing the country in terms of infrastructure and economic development,” he said.

Earlier, the Ogun State APC Chairman, Chief Yemi Sanusi, attributed the influx of opposition members into the party to the performance of the Abiodun administration.

Sanusi assured the defectors that they would enjoy the same rights and privileges as existing members, while urging other opposition members to join the ruling party and contribute to the development of the state.

In his remarks, Asiwaju Oladapo Odumosu, a former PDP member, thanked Governor Abiodun for accepting him and his supporters into the APC, saying the administration’s performance and its accommodating disposition encouraged their decision to leave the opposition.

Other defectors, including Messrs Ladi Owoduni, Damilola Talabi, Sesan Odufuwa from Odogbolu, Wale Adeyemi from Ijebu-North, Seun Oguntimeyin from Ijebu-North-East, Sunday Taiwo from Remo North, Adewale Ismael from Ijebu-Igbo and former ADC Chairman in Ijebu-North-East, Hon. Erinle Opeoluwa, described Abiodun as an accommodating administrator who treats people equally irrespective of political affiliation.

Rotimi Okenla, who contested for the Ogun State House of Assembly under the PDP in 2019, said after 17 years in the opposition, he decided to join the APC because of the performance and accommodating nature of the Abiodun administration.

The defectors pledged their loyalty to the APC and vowed to work for the party’s victory in the 2027 general elections.

World.title: Fubara Unveils 105-Bed Omoku Hospital, Targets Improved Healthcare in Rivers West
World.content:
Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt

Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, yesterday inaugurated the remodelled and fully furnished 105-bed Omoku Zonal Hospital in Ogba/Egbema/Ndoni Local Government Area, reaffirming his administration’s commitment to providing quality and accessible healthcare across the state.

Fubara, who spoke at the inauguration ceremony, said his administration places a premium on healthcare because unlike lost wealth that could be recovered, lost health was difficult to regain.

“If you lose wealth, you have lost nothing, because so long as you’re alive, opportunity might come back and you might gain what you have lost. If you lose your health, you have lost something. It’s not an easy thing to regain lost health,” he said.

The governor described healthcare, alongside the protection of lives and property and provision of essential services, as a fundamental responsibility of the government.

He said the hospital was strategically located to serve not only Omoku but also communities in Egbema, Ndoni, Ahoada and other parts of Rivers West Senatorial District.

“This facility is not just for Omoku. It is a facility that will also cater for the people of Egbema. It can also cater for the people of Ndoni, in serious cases. It can even take care of some part of people in this other side of Ahoada,” Fubara said.

The governor also urged residents, traditional rulers, chiefs and youths to protect the facility and its equipment from vandalism and theft, stressing that Omoku’s status as an oil and gas hub made the provision of quality healthcare particularly important.

“We need a good health service at this point in Omoku, considering the kind of developments that are coming up here. This is the oil and gas hub of our dear state,” he said.

Fubara said his administration would continue to complete projects to acceptable standards, urging the media and members of the public to avoid circulating unverified reports about government projects.

Inaugurating the project, the Oba of Ogbaland, Dr. Nwachukwu Nnam Obuoha Obi III, commended Fubara for executing what he described as tangible development projects across the area.

The monarch cited the recently inaugurated Elele-Omoku dual-carriageway and the completed Ahoada-Egbema road as evidence of renewed government presence in the area.

He also objected to describing the hospital merely as a remodelled facility, arguing that completing an abandoned project amounted to building it.

“I am not comfortable with those words, the choice of words. If you have started to build a house and you could not complete it, you have not done the job. He who completes a house is he who has built the house. That is why I’m comfortable to say: Thank you for building us a hospital,” he said.

The Permanent Secretary, Rivers State Ministry of Health, Dr. Vincent Wachukwu, said the three-storey secondary healthcare facility would serve as a referral centre for primary and secondary healthcare facilities across Rivers West, particularly in Ahoada East, Ahoada West, Ogba/Egbema/Ndoni, Emohua and parts of Ikwerre local government areas.

According to him, healthcare attendance in Ogba/Egbema/Ndoni increased by more than 200 per cent in three years, from about 58,914 patients to nearly 225,400 as of December 2025. He added that deliveries, skilled birth attendance and antenatal-care visits had also risen by about 20 per cent.

The hospital comprises outpatient clinics, pharmacy, accident and emergency services, surgical theatres, laboratories, intensive care and newborn intensive care units, paediatric, obstetrics and gynaecology wards, radiology services and private wards.

It also has a laundry, mortuary, kitchen and cafeteria, recreational garden, generator house, parking space for about 100 vehicles and staff accommodation.

Wachukwu said the government provided a 500kVA transformer, 350kVA and 150kVA generating sets, as well as a 90kVA solar power system with inverter batteries.

He said the facility would provide affordable secondary healthcare while supporting professional development, clinical training and medical student postings, thereby strengthening healthcare delivery and maternal, newborn and child health outcomes in the Orashi region.

World.title: Kwara APC Crisis Deepens as Mustapha Dumps Party, Picks PDP Ticket
World.content:
.Says he backs Tinubu

·Jiya, other aggrieved members follow as party reconciliation efforts falter

Hammed Shittu in Ilorin and Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

The crisis rocking the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kwara State has deepened ahead of the 2027 general elections following the resignation of the Senator representing Kwara Central Senatorial District, Saliu Mustapha, from the ruling party and his decision to pick the senatorial ticket of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP).

Mustapha, who chairs the Senate Committee on Agriculture and Rural Development, formally announced his resignation from the APC yesterday, ending weeks of speculation over his political future amid growing discontent within the party over the conduct and outcome of its recent governorship primary.

Also, another prominent APC member from Patigi Local Government Area, Hon. Kolo Jiya, has also resigned from the party and joined the PDP. Jiya is reportedly positioning himself to secure the PDP ticket for the Kwara North Senatorial District.

The latest defections followed earlier protests by 10 APC governorship aspirants who rejected what they described as the alleged imposition of the Speaker of the Kwara State House of Assembly, Salihu Yahaya Danladi, as Governor AbdulRazaq’s preferred candidate for the 2027 governorship election.

The aggrieved aspirants had raised concerns about the process through which the party’s governorship candidate emerged, further widening the divisions within the APC.

He said the coalition, which comprises members of the G15, Otoge Progressives (TOP) and the elders’ caucus, deliberately chose the PDP because it was considered the most suitable platform outside the APC for supporting Tinubu while challenging the ruling party’s structure in Kwara.

“I did not abandon the APC. But I have left the APC with a collective understanding. I’m representing the group in PDP so as to reset what AbdulRazaq thinks he wants to do,” he said.

According to him, the coalition emerged from the political crisis that followed the APC governorship nomination process, involving several aspirants who, he alleged, became alienated because of Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq’s style of running the party.

Mustapha listed some members and associates of the coalition to include Senator Yahaya Oloriegbe, Dele Belgore (SAN), Senator Lola Ashiru, Senator Sadiq Umar, among others.

THISDAY gathered that Mustapha has secured the PDP ticket to contest the Kwara Central senatorial seat in 2027, setting the stage for a major political battle with the APC candidate for the district, who is expected to be Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq.

His defection represents a major setback for the APC in the state and comes against the backdrop of widening disagreements among party members over the 2027 succession process and the outcome of the governorship primary.

The development also suggests that efforts to reconcile aggrieved members and contain the internal divisions within the party were yet to yield the desired result.

The APC had constituted a reconciliation committee following the controversies surrounding its primary election, but the initiative has failed to prevent some prominent members from seeking alternative political platforms ahead of the 2027 elections.

Mustapha’s departure is the latest in a series of developments exposing the depth of the crisis in the Kwara APC.

In his resignation letter to the APC leadership, Mustapha said his decision followed extensive consultations with political stakeholders, supporters and constituents across Kwara Central.

He said the decision was not taken lightly but became necessary following recent developments surrounding the party’s controversial governorship primary.

“This is not a decision I have taken lightly. It follows weeks of extensive consultations and engagements with relevant stakeholders, my supporters, constituents across Kwara Central Senatorial District, and well-meaning Kwarans,” he said.

Mustapha said his decision was guided by his belief that politics should remain centred on “people, principles and purpose.”

According to him, where a political platform no longer sufficiently aligns with those principles and the aspirations of the people he represents, “the honourable thing to do is to chart a new course.”

He maintained that his disagreement was with AbdulRazaq’s handling of the APC in Kwara and not with President Bola Tinubu, saying the coalition was determined to deliver the President at the national level while seeking to defeat the APC in the state.

“President Tinubu will even garner more votes this time around for himself. But at the state level, Tinubu will win at the national, while at the state, APC is a goner,” he declared.

He also dismissed reports that the Presidency had endorsed Speaker Yakubu Danladi-Salihu as the APC governorship candidate in Kwara.

“The Villa did not endorse Danladi as the candidate for us. Nothing like that. I’m 100 per cent sure because I’m an active participant in this process,” he said.

He thanked the national leadership of the APC led by President Tinubu, for the relationships and experiences he had gained during his years in the party.

“To the leadership of the APC, ably led by H.E. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, I express my deepest gratitude for the relationships and experiences I have been afforded over the years,” he said.

The senator assured his supporters and constituents that his decision to leave the APC would not affect his commitment to them.

“To my constituents, supporters, political associates and stakeholders in Kwara State and beyond, I assure you that while my political platform may change, my principles, my purpose and my commitment to the people remain unchanged,” he said.

He added, “I remain steadfast in my service to the people of Kwara Central, Kwara State and Nigeria at large.”

The senator also defended his record in office, citing the facilitation of 10 tractors, agricultural tricycles, electrification projects, transformers, medical facilities, school renovations, feeder roads and other federal interventions across Kwara Central.

Mustapha said he had prioritised agricultural production as a means of reducing poverty and supporting the Tinubu administration’s economic agenda.

He, however, rejected criticism over poverty in his senatorial district, arguing that his primary constitutional responsibilities were legislation and oversight, while the executive was responsible for creating the enabling environment, infrastructure and economic opportunities required to improve living standards.

On his alliance with former Senate President Bukola Saraki, Mustapha said it did not amount to abandoning Tinubu, stressing that Saraki, whom he described as the PDP leader in Kwara, was not contesting for any position in 2027.

He said the emerging “Rainbow Coalition” could produce an unusual political alignment in which PDP members would support Tinubu’s presidential bid while working to defeat the APC in Kwara.

“We want to reset the political mood in Kwara, so that not AbdulRahman or not Saliu Mustapha, anybody that comes there or that finds themselves there again, will not take everybody for granted,” he said.

The latest development has further complicated the APC’s preparations for the 2027 elections in Kwara, with the party now facing the challenge of managing its internal disagreements while preventing further defections of influential members.

For the PDP, however, the entry of Mustapha and other former APC members could significantly strengthen its chances of challenging the ruling party across the state’s three senatorial districts in the 2027 elections.

World.title: Former All Blacks star receiving death threats from Bok supporters
World.content:
Former All Blacks player Lima Sopoaga has opened up about receiving death threats from South Africans. Images via X

Former All Blacks player Lima Sopoaga has revealed that he has been receiving death threats from Springbok supporters following his commentary on the Greatest Rivalry series

The retired player is currently in South Africa to watch the rugby rivals play at Ellis Park on Saturday, 22 August.

Lima made his international debut for New Zealand in Johannesburg in 2015. In 2023, he qualified to play for Samoa through ancestry.



ALL BLACKS PLAYER RECEIVING DEATH THREATS FROM SPRINGBOK SUPPORTERS

On his social media account, former All Black Lima Sopoaga revealed that he had been on the receiving end of nasty comments, particularly from South African supporters.

He posted: “Hey guys, just remember it’s just a game. Some of you in my DMs, sending death threats and abusing the crap out of me because I said I want my team to win 2-1 in SA. I love a bit of banter and back-and-forth. But come on now, it’s not that deep”

During the Greatest Rivalry series taking place in South Africa, Lima has been sharing commentary about the All Blacks’ matches against provincial teams like the Stormers, Sharks and Bulls.



Like many rugby fans, he is particularly excited about the test match clash between the Kiwis and the Springboks, set to take place at Ellis Park.

Lima Sopoaga made his international debut for the All Blacks at the same stadium on 25 July 2015.

At the time, he was just 24 years old and was selected at No. 10 ahead of Beauden Barrett.



Lima played his last game for New Zealand in 2017 after signing to play club rugby in England.

Due to the selection policy, overseas-based players are not typically selected to represent the country. Fast forward to 2023, Lima Sopoaga swapped his All Blacks jersey for a Samoa jersey, thanks to his ancestry eligibility.

ELLIS PARK EXPERIENCE

It’s not the first frosty experience Lima Sopoaga has had in South Africa.



In 2015, he received a “hostile” reception from Springbok supporters when he made his All Blacks debut.

The New Zealand team won the match 27-20.

Lima said of the experience: “The whole day was surreal to be honest, it went by in a flash and felt like I’d played the game before it happened.



“On the way to the stadium, there were little kids throwing stuff at the bus and doing throat-cutting gestures. Old people were giving us the finger and yelling swear words, but playing in black was my dream come true”.

World.title: Boxing star Zolani Tete shot dead outside his home
World.content:
The 38-year-old Zolani Tete, affectionately known as “Last Born”, was ambushed at around 6:30 p.m. on Friday evening.

He was reportedly waiting for his residential gate to open when two armed suspects wearing balaclavas emerged from a vehicle and opened fire.

ZOLANI TETE WAS PREPARING FOR A BOXING COMEBACK

According to Eastern Cape police spokesperson Brigadier Nobuntu Gantana, Tete attempted to escape the hail of bullets by driving his vehicle into the yard. However, he suffered fatal injuries and was declared dead at the scene.



A 27-year-old woman who was travelling with him sustained multiple gunshot wounds. She was rushed to a nearby hospital, where she remains under medical care.

Tete’s longtime manager, Mlandeli Tengimfene, confirmed the devastating news and said the boxer’s next-of-kin had been informed.

The tragedy comes just weeks after Tete’s four-year anti-doping suspension officially expired on 29 July 2026. The southpaw had tested positive for stanozolol following his 2022 victory over Jason Cunningham.

Despite the setback, Tete was determined to return to the ring. His management team had confirmed that he was training for a comeback fight scheduled for 28 November 2026, with the ambitious goal of winning a third world title.

Instead, his career has been brought to a tragic end.

Tete leaves behind an extraordinary boxing legacy. He won the IBF junior-bantamweight world title in 2014 and held it until 2015 before becoming WBO bantamweight world champion between 2017 and 2019.



He also etched his name into the Guinness World Records when he stopped Siboniso Gonya in just 11 seconds during their 2017 world title fight in Belfast. It remains the fastest knockout in a world title fight.

SOUTH AFRICA MOURNS A BOXING ICON

Zolani Tete finished his professional career with 29 victories from 34 fights, including 22 wins by knockout. His achievements made him one of the most decorated South African fighters of the modern era.

Tributes have already begun pouring in from political and sporting bodies. Many recognise Tete’s enormous contribution to boxing and his impact on the Eastern Cape.

Meanwhile, the South African Police Service (SAPS) has opened cases of murder and attempted murder. The motive for the shooting remains unknown, while no arrests have been made.

World.title: Orlando Pirates to face the same PSL club three times in seven days
World.content:
Orlando Pirates and Sekhukhune United will face each other three times in just seven days. The unusual sequence features two MTN8 semifinal clashes and a league encounter sandwiched between them.

It is a fixture list that gives neither side much time to forget about the other. By the end of August, the Buccaneers and Babina Noko could know almost everything about each other.

ORLANDO PIRATES AND SEKHUKHUNE UNITED HAVE NO ESCAPE

The first meeting takes place on 22 August 2026, when the Sea Robbers travel to Peter Mokaba Stadium for the first leg of the MTN8 semifinal.



Just three days later, the teams meet again. This time, the Buccaneers host Sekhukhune United at Orlando Stadium in a Betway Premiership fixture on 25 August.

Also read: Full list: 13th player leaves Orlando Pirates

The trilogy then concludes on 29 August, when the two sides return to action for the second leg of the MTN8 semifinal.

That means three matches, two competitions and only seven days between Orlando Pirates and Sekhukhune United. The fixture calendar has essentially decided that these two teams are not allowed to escape each other.

For the players and coaches, there will be little time to recover. For supporters, however, it promises to be a fascinating week of football.

22 August: MTN8 semifinal first leg – Peter Mokaba Stadium

MTN8 semifinal first leg – Peter Mokaba Stadium 25 August: Betway Premiership – Orlando Stadium

Betway Premiership – Orlando Stadium 29 August: MTN8 semifinal second leg.

Both teams must manage fatigue, injuries, squad rotation and tactical adjustments while competing for an advantage in two different competitions. Every match could also provide the opponent with valuable information for the next encounter.



NEW SEASON START

For Orlando Pirates, the week comes at a time when the defending MTN8 champions have made an impressive start to the 2026/27 campaign.

The Buccaneers currently sit at the top of the Betway Premiership with seven points from three matches. They opened their league campaign with a 2-0 victory over Milford FC, before drawing 1-1 with AmaZulu FC and then defeating Chippa United FC 3-0.

Their cup defence also started positively. Orlando Pirates needed extra time to overcome Durban City FC 2-1 in the quarter-finals and book their place in the last four.

Sekhukhune United, meanwhile, have collected six points from their opening three league matches under coach Cedric Kaze.

Babina Noko started with a narrow 1-0 victory over Durban City FC, before suffering a 2-0 defeat to Kaizer Chiefs FC. They responded strongly by beating Polokwane City FC 2-0.

Their MTN8 campaign has arguably been even more dramatic. Sekhukhune United produced a thrilling 4-3 extra-time victory over AmaZulu FC in the quarter-finals to secure their semifinal place.

World.title: Two-division boxing world champion Zolani Tete shot dead
World.content:
MDANTSANE - Former two-time boxing world champion Zolani Tete has been shot and killed in Mdantsane, Eastern Cape.

Eastern Cape police spokesperson Brigadier Nobuntu Gantana confirmed that a shooting incident happened on Friday night at around 6:30pm.

According to Gantana, the 38-year-old male victim was arriving at his residence and waiting for the gate to open when he and a 27-year-old female passenger were ambushed by two unknown armed suspects, wearing balaclavas.

She said the suspects emerged from a vehicle and opened fire on them.

"In an attempt to escape the hail of bullets, the deceased drove his vehicle into the yard. He unfortunately succumbed to his injuries and was declared deceased on the scene." "The female passenger sustained multiple gunshot wounds and was immediately rushed to a nearby hospital for medical treatment. She remains hospitalised," Gantana said.

The circumstances surrounding the incident are still unknown as investigations continue.

"At this stage, no arrests have been made...The suspects fled the scene and are yet to be apprehended," she said.

Tete formerly held the WBF Flyweight and WBO Bantamweight titles.

He was expected to return to the ring shortly.

READ | Promoter says Joshua will return to ring when 'time is right' after horror crash

Following a fourth-round knockout victory over Jason Cunningham in 2022, Tete tested positive for the steroid stanozolol.

This resulted in the UK Anti-Doping agency issuing him a mandatory four-year ban from boxing.

He was said to be planning a return to the ring following the expiration of his suspension in July 2026.

World.title: 'Duck run' pest control catching on in South Africa's winelands
World.content:
STELLENBOSCH - Every morning, around 1,000 long-necked ducks are let loose on a South African wine farm to gobble up insects in an environmentally friendly method of pest control that is gaining popularity.

At 9am, the upright and flightless Indian Runner ducks charge out of their pens on a farm near the Stellenbosch wine-producing area outside Cape Town and head to work.

After a rapid but brief forage for aphids, worms and snails near the homestead and restaurant, they move into the vineyards for the rest of the day.

"Using the ducks instead of pesticides is obviously better for the ecology," said Vergenoegd Low Wine Estate and farm manager, Christiaan Cloete.

"When you use chemicals, you sometimes kill a lot of beneficial insects. We are trying to create a more biodiverse ecology in the vineyards," Cloete told AFP.

The farm introduced the practice around 40 years ago.

"It's beginning to pick up in popularity," he said, as farmers seek more sustainable and biologically friendly methods, including "regenerative farming" which aims to restore degraded soil.

Now between five and 10 surrounding farms purchase ducks from the farm, Cloete said.

- Looking after the soil -

There are around 890 ducks on the property with 400 hatchlings expected over the breeding season from mid-July to the end of October, Cloete said.

Half will be sold and the rest will replace the more senior ducks on the farm's own fleet.

Indian Runner ducks were originally bred in Indonesia to control pests in rice paddies, said the farm's ecology ranger, Milan Germishuizen.

Their long necks allow them to reach pests on the raised, trellised vines.

They are also handy in breaking down the manure of the 220 sheep and nearly 100 cattle that graze in the vineyard, another regenerative farming practice that leaves the soil nutrient-rich.

"The more pesticides and artificial fertilisers you put onto your soil, eventually your soil will degenerate," he said.

"So by using natural methods ... we are really looking after our soils, which eventually does give us a much better product at the end of the day."

When there are grapes on the vines, the ducks are kept away to avoid them being tempted by the fruit, and diverted to the four irrigation dams.

As they forage there, their droppings enrich the water in a process called "fertigation", Germishuizen said.

"A lot of our neighbours have gotten on board with regenerative farming," said Tessa Kleynhans, the commercial manager of the on-site hotel.

The impressive daily duck run has also become a draw for visitors, she told AFP.

"We're trying to set the precedent for regenerative farming. We are trying to make a use case that, if you invest the capital in the beginning, even though it's a long, tedious process, it is worth it in the end," she said.
